utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Registrar, kindly call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-74-T, the Prosecutor versus Prlic et al. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, registrar. Today we are Tuesday the 2nd of October 2007. I'd like to greet the representatives of the Prosecution, Defence counsel, the accused and all the people giving us a helping hand. It so happens that due to an error in our calculations, the Prosecution has had 20 minutes less than it should have. Therefore, the Prosecutor was not able to introduce some of the documents he wished to so we have a very simple solution to this. After the cross-examination, and as part of the redirect, the Prosecution will be able to adduce those documents that are connected to the questions raised in the cross-examination, and if necessary, ask for these documents to be tendered by making submissions in writing. As we have a little extra time, once we will have completed the cross-examination by Mr. Kovacic defending -- and Mr. Praljak, and Mr. Stojic's Defence team, I will give the floor to Mrs. Alaburic again so that she can ask a few additional questions. But if her questions will have been raised by other Defence counsel, then that will not be the case. Much will depend on what happens here this morning. Then the Prosecution will have time for redirect and can adduce new documents if need be. This is how we are going to proceed this morning. Would it be at all possible if we were to finish earlier than expected, could we hear the next witness today, Mr. Poryvaev?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm not sure because the witness came a little bit later yesterday, not in the morning, and he has been working with our assistants preparing for the trial. I don't think it's possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President, Your Honours. In relation to the error in calculation that the Prosecution have been given 20 minutes less, it's our respectful submission that the error should be remedied at the earliest possible opportunity. Of course, the Prosecution is master of its own examination-in-chief and it may well be the case that the questions asked go beyond merely admitting documents, but they would perfectly be within their rights to ask questions on substantive issues. In order to prevent proceedings becoming a jack in a box with then the Defence seeking to stand up and cross-examine on those new issues, it seems sensible, in our respectful submission, that as we are yet to start the next cross-examination for the Defence, that my learned friend now, at this juncture, continues his cross-examination -- examination-in-chief and then we cross-examine as normal afterwards. Your Honours, that's our respectful submission.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence of General Petkovic supports that proposal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For once a Defence counsel agree with what the Prosecution has said. We then feel that the Prosecution can take the floor. Defence counsel feel that there might have been important questions which you would have liked to put to the witness, and in that case, if those questions have not been put, this might prejudice you, as we have quite a lot of time today and 20 minutes is not much of an issue. We entitle you to put other questions to the witness for 20 minutes. So we shall drop the blinds and bring the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: [Representative of Spanish government entered court].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We shall move into closed session again. So as to be able to display the logo.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Prosecution, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: I will take an opportunity in proposing some rectifications in the transcript because I noticed there were some mistakes. First of all, page 33, line we should read Exhibit P02570. The same page, 33, line 19, we should read instead of P0 -- P0502582, we should read P02582. That's my rectifications to the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I see that that last but one figure is P0502582 and that -- although we have many documents that I think is a bit too much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes. I agree but we have corrected. It should be read P02582. Okay. It's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Sorry, I'm getting a little bit lost.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Poryvaev, yesterday I noticed that we had this very long number, a great number of digits. I did not say anything because I think it was obvious to everyone that you were talking about 02582, but you are quite right to mention it and to give us the right number. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Further examination by Mr. Poryvaev:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, yesterday we started talking about Ljubuski, but due to lack of time we had to wind it up and finish at some point and I've -- now I would like to address you to your -- to logbook entry of the 15th of August 1993. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Here we have that you had contacts with UNHCR to discuss the problem of expulsion of 150 Muslims from the area of Ljubuski. Is it correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DV [Resumed]
utterances.text: What this information reflects is that members of my section were at that meeting with the UNHCR, yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the following day, on the 16th of August, UNCIVPOL and UNHCR requested the presence during the night in the village of Gradska where there were 50 Muslim families, 250 women, children and elderly, 92 men of aged between 18 and 60 taken to Heliodrom. And you just stated that you at some point got involved in this problem. What were your actions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DV [Resumed]
utterances.text: In theory, this was quite established practice. The UNHCR requested, because they needed the information, the support of UNPROFOR for technical reasons. In practice, I seem to recall that they requested that there be a military presence in that town that night, and I don't remember very well but I think that that presence was provided. I don't remember the details. But my mission was to analyse the request from the UNHCR, and we decided to provide the information to UNCIVPOL and everything necessary was done so that this would be carried out. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now I will turn you to Exhibit P04214. This is binder 3. English page 3. 04214.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have it before me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Here we have that on the 15th of August, the section received information concerning the expulsion of Muslims. Is it the same information you've just told the Trial Chamber about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I understand that this concerns the same information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And let's go back to the 24th of August, to your logbook, where you stated that on that day, 24th of August you received information that over 800 Muslim refugees, mainly women, children, elderly have been taken by the HVO to the Vrdi zone in buses, and forced to come towards Dreznica, Muslim zone, and I would like now -- we discussed it yesterday, but I just used to these entry just to remind you of the situation. And now I would like you to turn to Exhibit P04472, 4472, binder 3?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DV [Resumed]
utterances.text: M'hm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is page 5 English and page 2 Spanish.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I have the document before me. I confirm that this is an official document which is INTREP 352 from the 24th of August and it states that there is a reconnaissance patrol from SpaBat there and this was patrolling in the region of Dreznica, and there we had about 1.000 refugees, mostly women, children and elderly heading towards Dreznica taken by HVO. Currently, transport is being conducted outside of the area. Another INTREP confirms this information. It was quite frequent for patrols in the region to come across groups of civilians who had left an area of conflict, escaping fire, and therefore, the patrols would try to deal with any requests for help at that time. This was mainly -- I remember one particular case where there was a child wounded by a bullet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then you have Exhibit P04623, binder 3. This is INTREP 278, dated 29th of August 1993. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have found it. I have found the document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you authenticate this document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I authenticate this document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then here we have today about 600 refugees crossed Dreznica-Vrdi confrontation line, men aged 20 and 70, they look pathetic and show signs of starvation. They come from the prisons of Dretelj, Gabela and Prozor. According to BiH army a group of 1500 refugees had to cross the confrontation line at Slatina. My question is here we have 29th of August and before we just discussed the situation with just Muslims on the 24th August. Perhaps we can clarify, was it the same group or -- of Muslims mentioned on the 24th and 29th or different?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Before the gentleman answers the question, just for technical purposes, is there a foundation? The gentleman is authenticating documents saying that this is an official document. It then goes on to read the document as if he was present there, as if he had generated the document, and then says well, this is what happened. In other words he's reading hear say and then he's authenticating not just the document but also the content as if the content is true, accurate and complete. Now the same thing is happening on the 29th of August. My question is was the gentleman present? Does he have any firsthand knowledge? Otherwise the document speaks for itself. He authenticates the document, the document comes in, you may need to bring in another witness to discuss the content. But unless he has personal knowledge I would object to the gentleman simply reading a document and saying this is what happened. I'm not suggesting that --

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Your Honour, could I explain? I'm sorry. Yesterday, I showed the witness his logbook. All these dates. And number of Muslims were mentioned, and now I ask questions in development of my yesterday questions. He confirmed the entries in his logbook.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If the gentleman can confirm that he was present and has actual knowledge, we can move on. Otherwise, I don't think it's very beneficial to have someone read official documents and then verify the contents of the documents unless he has some sort of independent knowledge of it. That's all I'm saying Your Honour, and I think that's called a foundation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will put the question to him directly. Witness, this document, 4623, bears INTREP number 278. This document was drafted on the 12th of August 1993. So my question is a very simple one: When you were at the time fulfilling your function, did you see this document, INTREP 278.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course. All the documents that came from the 2nd or 3rd section were distributed to all the other sections. So that all the circumstances would be known to all units. So hours after its drafting I was aware of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the time, had you read this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, yes, it was my duty to do it and I did it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So everything mentioned in this document was something which you had direct or indirect knowledge of at the time; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Please proceed, Mr. Poryvaev.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Thanks, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just, witness, I would like to you answer my question. My question was, was it the same group of detainees that was seen on the 29th of August?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DV [Resumed]
utterances.text: What has to be understood is that this was a different group. It wasn't the same group because we are talking about different dates. The INTREPs, which are intelligence reports, cover one specific day or a specific time frame and so it reflects that particular point in time. So I understand, when I read these two differently dated documents, that they refer to two different groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay, may we get some clarification? Is the gentleman then speaking from personal actual knowledge or is it something that is inferred from the document itself? Which of the two? And that's my -- that was the purpose of my objection, Your Honour. Because the documents do speak for themselves. We don't need to have the Prosecutor read the document to us. We can read them and I know where he's going but -- so that was my objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Sir, when I put you the question -- when I put the question to you whether you had direct or indirect knowledge of this, I anticipated that Defence counsel would react this way. So what can you say to respond to what has just been said? Was this direct or indirect knowledge? Was this something you heard about because somebody told you? Did you learn it from hear say or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, obviously not the whole section is on the confrontation line. This is information which comes from certain officers who were present at the confrontation line. This comes from the appropriate channels and is reflected in the second section which was then distributed to the other sections but I cannot, for example, say whether there, the state of the prisoners was pathetic because I didn't see it with my own eyes. What I can say is that the information came to us via the second section on the day. Now why did we receive this information? Because our duty was to inform the NGOs, part of our duty to understand the situation on the ground and inform the NGOs, but I was not part of that group. If that is what the Defence counsel's question is, because I was -- I did not actually see it with my own eyes, if that answers your question, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My next question is let's go back to logbook, 8th of September, and this is page 44 -- maybe it's Spanish -- they say that on that day SpaBat participated in the negotiations to evacuate 300 displaced persons. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. I've found it. I think it's page 50 in the Spanish version. The 8th of September, in the sixth paragraph they are talking about managing the 100 displaced people towards Patkovinca [phoen] yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry, one moment, I'm sorry. The last paragraph "Negotiations to evacuate 300 displaced persons," yes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's correct. I identify this as an entry in the logbook of the section. I can clarify that I personally did not perform this management because I was involved in the aerial evacuation of individuals from Mostar, but I can say that I was involved also in the solution of medicines problems in the region of Mostar. I had had that written in my personal diary. So I can confirm that this document is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. My next question, let's take a look at Exhibit P04870. This is binder 3. English page 7. Have you found this document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. The document, yes, but now I have to find the page. What page was it, I beg your pardon?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Page 4 in Spanish.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. This is a document which has the 289 INTREP which corresponds to the date 8 of September, yes. Yes, and here in the third point, under miscellaneous, other information they talk about some 300 refugees hoping that they can be evacuated the following day when the HVO enables this to be possible, and then they were saying that it would be a question of days before the HVO secures the area. So this was a technical analysis of what was happening in situ at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Next Exhibit, 04905, binder 1. INTREP 290, dated 9th of September 1993. English page 3, Spanish page 4. Topic Jablanica. They state here that "This morning SpaBat evacuated refugees." Do you know about this fact?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I recall that this evacuation took place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And my final question, Your Honour, now I will turn you to your personal diary, to the 9th of June.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. 9th of June?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you preside over a meeting in Medjugorje? They are talking about in this document? What kind of meeting was it and what issues were discussed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. In theory, every week, on a certain set days, but also in case of need when there was a relevant event, all the representatives from all of the organisations would meet in Medjugorje to have a briefing about the situation. In that meeting the technical situation was discussed. Risks were also presented. What were the statutes or the statuses of the roads and any other relevant information for the NGOs, and I presided over that meeting. In this particular case on the 9th of June we expounded a major problem which was in the Vlata [phoen] region. It hadn't been -- it had been difficult at that time to reach a compromise among all of the organisations so that humanitarian aid could be delivered to that region because the NGOs were saying that until there was a cease-fire, they could not bring the aid. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You are talking about the 9th of June but in the document we are talking about the 9th of July, witness. Can you please confirm this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the Spanish document that I have before me, in my personal diary, we are talking -- if we are talking about the same document, we are talking about the personal diary, is that so? It is the 9th of 6, Your Honour. In my personal diary. As I said, I carried my personal diary to remind myself of what was happening in every day -- well, thank you for that but I was talking about, that I understand that in the English version, it needs to be corrected.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, please could you repeat the region? Because it didn't come out in the transcript, the region of the problem you were discussing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The official region that we knew was Donja Mahala neighbourhood, the Donja Mahala neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then I will turn you to Exhibit 02593. I think that it should be binder 2. 02593. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I've found the document. I'm looking at the Spanish part. This document is an INTREP 139, dated on the 23rd of May -- sorry, INTREP 189.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry, the date, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's the 23rd of May, quite come -- sorry, the 31st of May at the end of the day, it was written. I'm referring to 2593, is that correct? Or have I got the wrong document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: SpaBat INTREP 189, yes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, INTREP 189, page 3, yes, I have it before me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "The town council of Muslim quarter Donja Mahala have sent a letter." Have you found this document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. It discusses the situation. It talks about the council Chambers of Donja Mahala and its negotiations with SpaBat in which we are trying to -- 2500 displaced people. These people were accommodated in -- these refugees were accommodated in council Chambers.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Your Honour. This was my final question. Thank you very much for your generosity and patience.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Ms. Alaburic, you may want to resume, since the Prosecution dealt with some new subjects. You have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, does that mean that I may continue my cross-examination before my colleagues carried out their cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, normally you could continue with your cross-examination but related to the questions raised in the last 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I will not have any additional questions related to the questions raised in the last 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As for the rest, Ms. Alaburic, you needed how many minutes for the remainder of your cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In view of the fact that we are losing a relatively large amount of time on interpretation, I think up to 40 minutes would be sufficient for me to complete my cross-examination, but I will be satisfied with less if any time remains after my colleagues are finished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Ibrisimovic do you wish to proceed on the basis of the new questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. We have no intention of putting additional questions. MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC: [Interpretation] We do not have additional questions either, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Let us proceed with the cross-examinations. Mr. Karnavas?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President, good morning, Your Honours. Good morning everyone in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good morning, sir. I have just have a very few questions to ask. Hopefully in five minutes we can get through this. Now, I'm going to be referring to the statement that you gave on the 2nd, 3rd and 6th of July 2007. I believe that's Prosecution document P10217. Now, if we look at paragraph 161 -- incidentally I should have introduced myself. My name is Michael Karnavas. With me is Mrs. Ana Tomanovic, and we represent Dr. Jadranko Prlic; hence why we're going to paragraphs 161 and 165. So if we could start of with 165 and then we'll go to 161. In your statement you say on August -- "On the 24th of August, we stated in our summary that a high level meeting was held between my commander, Mr. Thornberry bring, Prime Minister Prlic, Bruno Stojic and Jerry Hume." Now, just to make sure that I'm clear on this, you did not attend that particular meeting; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. I organised the meeting but my president -- my commander was there, Mr. Thornberry and the other names were there so that's correct. I did not actually discuss the issues there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. There is documentation, I suspect, concerning that particular meeting. But as far as you know -- well, let me ask you this: Were you debriefed afterwards concerning that particular meeting? Did you get a debriefing from your superior, your commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Naturally. Not only that but I also had orders to organise a convoy.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Very well. Now, let's go back to 161 now, paragraph 161. I just want to clarify one point here. Here, it's unclear whether we are talking about the 19th, the 20th, or the 21st of August. But you talk about a meeting after a meeting with Prlic and Thornberry an agreement was reached and eventually they gave permission so that on Friday a convoy could go through. Now, again, let me ask this question. Were you present at this particular meeting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DV [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. On the 19th, the date is there to describe the process. On the 19th I met with Mr. Thornberry, I met with him officially, and then we organised the convoy with supplies on the 20th. On the 21st, we prepared the convoy. In this meeting with Thornberry and Mr. Prlic I wasn't there. I wasn't of a high enough level to be present.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I'm wondering how is it that you place Mr. Prlic at this meeting? Because if I look at your diary, and we're talking about document P10269, and we go to page 10 of it in English, what we have is the 19th, the 20th, and the 21st, you have some entries there, there is no mention of Mr. Prlic. On the 20th of August, for instance, you note that there was some sort of a meeting between Mr. Thornberry, Mr. Benabou, Mr. Stojic, Mr. Bozic, where there was a discussion of the UN convoy with medical aid for Mostar. But as you would -- you would agree with me there is no Mr. Prlic either on the 19th, 20th or 21st?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, to solve this problem, Mr. Karnavas, you have the Exhibit 4472, which shows, on page 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: 4472, Mr. President, is regards August 24th. That was the document that the gentleman was shown. But we are talking about August 19th, 20th or 21st, and since the gentleman has it in his diary -- in his statement, this is why I'm asking the question is how is it that he's placing Mr. Prlic at a particular meeting when in the document, in the exhibit, which is 10269, the gentleman's diary itself, there is no mention -- there is an August 20th, we see, he says that he participated together with Mr. Thornberry, Mr. Benabou, Mr. Stojic, and Mr. Bozic in a meeting which discussed plans for UN convoy with medical aid for Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you see that, sir? Sir, I'm asking you a question if you could be so kind as to just direct your full attention to my question as opposed to looking at documents?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, yes, please, look at the counsel and then you can look for the document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Like in the army we have to abide by orders and there is a particular order -- [Speakers overlapping]

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand perfectly. I thank you for mentioning my personal diary because I usually put things in my personal diary that I'm personally involved in. In the logbook, on the 20th of August, the first -- one moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Excuse me, excuse me, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Excuse me, sir. Here I'm the commanding officer, and I'm giving the orders, and I'm asking to you look at the document? One document at --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: My way not your way, okay? Now, I don't mean to be aggressive but I'm trying to just do my job. And I'm not going to let you do what you did yesterday to Mrs. Alaburic, I'm sorry. So in your personal diary, looking at 20th August, there is no mention of Mr. Prlic there, yes or no, just answer that question, and then we'll go step by step. I'm not going to mislead you, sir.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honour, that I have to do as the Defence is asking.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Obviously, in my personal diary there is no reference, you're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you. And may I remind you that when you came in here, the president instructed you on how the direction is going to be -- how we question over here, okay? So I understand that you might be used to a different system in Spain or wherever else you may come from, but this is the procedure. Please abide by it. Now, if we look at the next document, which is P2108, now, that's the daily information summary, you see, we are going to go step by step. I'm going to be very fair to you, sir. Now, if we go, for instance, to August 24th, which would be on page 39, we clearly see that there was a meeting, and we clearly see that Mr. Prlic is at that meeting on the 24th. On the 24th. Okay? Which is page 39 of English. Now, if we -- and the reason I'm pointing at the 24th because clearly we can see that, you know, even though you indicated you were not at that meeting on the 24th, we have a document which was referred to earlier, 4472, now we look at this document, P2108, and we clearly we can connect the dots and show that on the 24th, Mr. Prlic was at this meeting. Now, if we look earlier, you see, this is why there was no need for you to look for it because I've already done the work for you, if you look at the 19th and the 20th, on the 20th, for instance, we see that there are some meetings, we see some names. You would agree with me, sir, would you not, at least in the English part on page 38, there is no Mr. Prlic at any meeting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DV [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is correct. He's not mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but, Witness, did you say at some point in time that Mr. Prlic had taken part in a meeting on the 20th of August?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know whether I said it or not. I don't think I have enough elements to say that he was there that day. We know that Mr. Thornberry had high level meetings, but I don't know because I can't see anywhere that the meeting was with Mr. Prlic. If that is the question. Right now, I don't remember or I don't know what the dates were. Many things happened at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We are now going to proceed. Now who is it? Whose turn is it? I can't remember. Mr. Kovacic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, it is Ms. Nozica, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sorry, Mrs. Nozica.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Good morning, sir. I'm Defence counsel together with my colleague, Karim Khan, for Mr. Stojic. And yesterday, I noticed that in the courtroom, there was somebody who for once speaks faster than I do because I've been accused of speaking very, very fast. So I'd like to ask you to slow down, both of us to slow down, to give the interpreters a chance and not make it a problem for them. In your statement of July 2007, and that is document P0217, you don't have to look at the document, I will ask you to focus on the parts I would like to deal with. I hope that the witness has a copy of my binder and that everybody else in the courtroom does too, the Prosecution, Their Honours. So we are referring to statement P10217, but as I say there is no need for you to look at it. You can listen to my questions, and I'll tell you when you need to look at the document. Anyway, in paragraph 113 to 120, you spoke about the contacts you had with Mr. Bruno Stojic, with respect to the release of four interpreters, Muslim interpreters, associates or, rather, assistants of the military observers, and of the International Red Cross, the UNHCR, who were kidnapped on the 16th of June 1993 in the Konjic pocket. Now, sir, in the courtroom, we've discussed this topic very many times. However, we now have someone here who took part in this directly and that person is you. So I would like to go through certain matters and clarify certain things step by step, and I don't think there will be any problems there. In paragraph 113 of your report, you said the following: You said, on the 17th of June, I had contact with Minister Stojic, during six hours of negotiations in which I had to pressure him to free four Muslim interpreters. That's what it says, word by word. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, in paragraph 120 of that same statement, you say the following: "I would not say that Stojic, as a commander, was not able to solve the problem with the interpreters. He simply did not have the means of communication in order to make proper and sharp or convey proper and sharp decisions and also, according to what he said, the Croats from Konjic acted independently." Have I stated that correctly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DV [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Sir, let's try and clear up some things together, some of the observations you make in your statement, and they are the following: What pressure did you exert on Mr. Stojic for six hours? Was this kind of pressure necessary? Just listen to me. Let me finish. Was he the commander? And the third point is this: Was it only according to his statement that the Croats in the Konjic pocket acted independently? Now, through my following questions and the documents we are going to look at, I'm sure we'll arrive at answers to all those three questions. Now, my first question is this: Did you know that the UNHCR, on the 16th of June 1993, immediately upon the arrest of these interpreters, sent a request for their release to the Office of the President of HZ HB, who was Mr. Boban? Did you know that? Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORYVAEV
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think the witness is completely lost because I see at least four questions put in a run. Which one should be answered now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Nozica, please try to ask one question at a time, otherwise it's difficult to keep track.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think I said it clearly enough but I'll repeat. We have three questions, three things we are challenging, and we'll arrive at the answers step by step.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, the question that I'm asking the witness now is this: Did he know, was he aware of the fact that the UNHCR on the 16th of June straight away, after the interpreters were arrested, sent in a request for their release to the Office of the President of the HZ HB?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DV [Resumed]
utterances.text: My answer is no, I didn't -- I wasn't aware of that situation.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Let's now look at a document. It is P02793, and it is a document you'll find in my binder which is the pink binder. Is that it? I see you've taken it out of the pink binder but it is the third document from the top. Tell me when you've found it, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I found the document. I have the English version.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: For the Trial Chamber, I'd just like to say that you have yellow stickers which mark the documents having the status of exhibit, so as you say, this is a document you've never seen before. You're looking at it for the first time now. Now would you look at its contents, please? Look at the first page of the document, and although it has exhibit status, this first page has not been translated but it's easy to conclude that we are dealing with the 16th of June, that that is the date, and that this document was sent to Mr. Bruno Stojic and Bruno Pesic [phoen] and it says at the bottom, "Mr. President, I would like to hear your stand with regards to this issue of Vlado Pogarcic," and then it says "urgent" underneath. Did you ever meet Mr. Vlado Pogarcic, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DV [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't know that person.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Nozica, there may be a mistake. You said that this document was sent to Mr. Petkovic. I'm looking at the people who were supposed to receive it. There is Boban, General Petkovic, Mr. Prlic, SpaBat and ECMM. I can't see the name of Mr. Stojic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in the original document, it says to Mr. Pogarcic in person and at the bottom it says who it was also sent out to. Now, in an attending letter, and this is a Prosecution document, this is it, it is an additional document attached to the first, and it says that the Office of the President sent this copy to Mr. Stojic, in the cover letter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And that was not translated; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right. Your Honour, this has the status of exhibit but this page has not been translated. That's quite right. We'll see about that in due course because that was an omission when the exhibit was admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Anyway, sir, you don't know that it reached the Presidency so let's move on. Let's look at your report, P02794, dated the 16th of June 1993. It is in the Prosecution binder on page 4 of both the English and Croatian versions. 02794 is a document that you were shown yesterday by the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to refer to two points to see if you can confirm them. It is your report, right, dated the 16th of June? And it says that this report relates to a period ranging between the 15th of June, 1830 hours, to the 16th of June, 1830 hours. On page 4, it says, well, we are dealing with the 16th of June, and I'm referring to the portion related to Jablanica-Konjic. It says that it seems that the HVO soldiers who captured the interpreters did this without the knowledge of the commander of that pocket, who previously had meetings with the presidents because they even threatened the HVO escorts that was -- escort that was with them. Now, on the second page, after the names of these interpreters, it says that contact was established with the HVO and that two letters were prepared from General Lasic and Mr. Stojic, and that at 845 hours a Jablanica platoon received orders to take the letters and try to have the prisoners released. Therefore, sir, can we agree that from this report, it follows that you, already on the 16th of June, straight after these interpreters had been captured, concluded that this capture was most probably perpetrated without the knowledge of the commander of the pocket? Would that be right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DV [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Furthermore, from this report, it would follow that, already on the 16th of June, so that same day, when the interpreters were arrested, General Lasic and Mr. Stojic sent two letters to the commander of the Konjic pocket requesting that the interpreters be released. Is that also correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's correct. I don't know whether request is the right word or to order. I don't know that. In the translation of his words, I don't know whether to say, "Request" or "order" would be the right word, to order the release or to request the release. I'm not quite sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Well, for the moment, well, your intervention is in order but we'll get to that. We'll deal with who can issue an order and who can issue a request. We'll come to that in due course. Let's look at your report now, once again it was shown by the Prosecutor, it is in the Prosecution binder, P02804. It is also a report dated the 16th of June 1993. But it was -- the time is 2250 hours, and I'd like to focus on what it says on page 2 of that document. So it's a report written on the same day but later on that day, and it says, I'm looking at the routes and then the subtitle, information, and it says, and once again refers to the arrest, when the meeting was finished, a group of HVO soldiers, it seems without the knowledge of their commander, threatened by force of arms and captured and once again all the four names, all the four commanders are mentioned, and then it goes on to say that SpaBat, in the area, brigadiers Lasic and Stojic, and Mr. Stojic promised that he would release them the following day. Now, sir, you've read the report. You know what it's about. From this report, we can see once again that this was perpetrated by a group of soldiers without the knowledge of the commander of the pocket and that Mr. Stojic acted immediately after he learned of their arrest and took steps; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DV [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Let us now look once again at the Prosecution document P02808 dated the 17th of June, and the time is 1830 hours. It's in the Prosecution binder. Tell me when you've found the document.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've found it.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I'm referring to what it says on page 4 of both the Croatian and the English versions. Now, sir, here we have a whole sequence of events under the heading, "Jablanica" and you say, we are talking about the date, it's very important, the date was the 17th of June, and you say that steps were taken to release the interpreters, the headquarters of the HVO was contacted, and as the result of that, they issued an order for release. They decided to send Zarko, Keza, to the Konjic pocket and after that, it says that the Bosnian army, the BH army, did not authorise his passage through their territory. And that's why he wasn't able to pass through. Then it says at 1300 hours, in Masat, two in Masat telephone lines were placed at the disposal of the command of the Konjic pocket and the HVO Minister of Defence, Stojic, for communication to be established. When it was established, Commander Zuhric that's where it says here, told the captain of SpaBat that he would receive an answer with respect to the release or non-release of the prisoners at 1700 hours. At 1700 hours, the communication was established once again and it was said that they would reach an agreement by 1700 hours the following day, and then a final attempt was made at 1830 hours of that same day. This is a report dated the 17th of June, when you, in your report, stated that you held negotiations with Mr. Stojic and the negotiations lasted for six hours, during which you had to exert pressure on him to release the four interpreters. Now, sir, from this report, can we see that Mr. Bruno Stojic did not have any communication links, was not able to come into contact with the HVO, members of the HVO, in the Konjic pocket?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DV [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this is not right. He established communication with the head of the pocket of Konjic; i.e., the pressure I exerted and the pressure that we had to do, if you allow me to explain myself, is that the letters were no good, didn't have any effect.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You didn't understand me, sir. It is indisputable that he did establish contact. Please follow what I'm saying. But did he have the means to do so, the means of communication? Or was it up to you to ensure the means of communication? I'm not challenging the fact that contact was established, but did he have the means to do so or did he have to do it through you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, surprisingly, we discovered that they didn't have or that's what they told us, they didn't have any means of communication with the pocket of Konjic which surprised us. So the decision that I suggested to my head was that UNPROFOR provided a means, the radio of UNPROFOR which was the situation completely not normal at all. But we thought it was important in order to manage to get these people, these four people, released. And they had been captured for two days already. So he said that he didn't have those means. So we tried to solve the problem with the means that were at our disposal, after letters and after trying to have the head of the counter-intelligence involved, i.e., after certain actions that we didn't think that the Minister of Defence had to do. So what he had to do was to issue orders, not to request. He had to issue an order in order for these people to be released. And to have the head of the counterintelligence involved through -- well, wasn't acceptable by the Armija, and they didn't accept this solution, so there was a delay. And they were using the problem of the interpreters to obtain certain advantages. That is something that we couldn't -- we couldn't allow, as UNPROFOR. Our obligation was that the members of the Red Cross and other organisations weren't used in such a manner.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You said what you wanted to say, but we would have got to that point but let's take it step by step. From the report itself, it emerges that from the first to the last contact through the communication you enabled, that six hours elapsed; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, what I mean by these six hours is that there were not six hours in a row. Many things happened, many movements, many goings to the headquarters in order for them to see the importance for the international community of the release of these members. With Mr. Stojic or, well, when my commander asked me to go to the headquarters with the help of my interpreters, of course, and the pressure we were trying to exert was for him to realise that we had to be hasty and that there wasn't a lot of time at our disposal.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Sir, you're not answering my question once again. I understand your frustration, that that was a lot of time for you. But we are trying to establish now what it was that Mr. Stojic endeavoured to do, what he could have done, and whether he did everything that was asked of him. I understand that as far as you were concerned, it was a long time, but we are trying to establish what the facts were. What he had at his disposal, who listened to him, who didn't listen to him, whether you were satisfied with that amount of time, I'm clear on the fact that you were not, but please try and focus on what Mr. Stojic did do during that period of time. Now, you were present during this communication, this special line between Mr. Stojic and the representative in the Konjic pocket, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was there, and with the help of my interpreter, he was trying to tell me what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You're not challenging the fact that Mr. Stojic demanded the commander of the pocket to release the interpreters, but the man refused to do so during those three conversations over the communication line while you were present?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, you were present with Mr. Stojic or with the pocket commander, Mr. Zaric? You were present with whom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, we went where our satellite was and Mr. Stojic picked up the phone and by means of satellite, he talked to the interpreter. Obviously, I didn't understand what they were saying but my interpreter well, gave me a summary of what he had said, and the -- and minister Stojic tried in several occasions to release -- for these prisoners to be released, and he also asked about the situation and, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. However, the commander of the Konjic pocket refused to do so, to release the interpreters, that is, during all those six hours and three contacts, conversations?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this was our impression and finally they were released, but it was very, very hard, for Mr. Stojic to make the pocket realise or the commander realise that it wasn't in the interest of the HVO to upkeep that situation. This is correct. I saw the pressure he tried to exert and this is what I reflect in my statement. As I said, everyone had their own activity calendars, if you will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: If I may, just to make sure, in your -- in your statement, one gets the feeling that you say you had to exercise a lot of pressure on Mr. Stojic, and now it seems that you say that Mr. Stojic exercised a lot of pression, and we have not heard much concretisation on what you yourself had to do as the means of pression.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Please allow me, because the -- the system of just answering yes or no just doesn't allow us to tell you about all the nuances. In my report, what we tried to tell Mr. Stojic or that whatever the letters that were sent or that the commander of conic doesn't take any notice, and even if we tried to have the head of the counter-intelligence of the HVO involved, for him to go personally to this pocket which is not accepted by the other part, well, that wasn't an excuse for him to issue an order to solve the problem for once and for all. So my pressure on the minister, who had many other important things to do on those dates, that wasn't the only thing in his agenda, was to make him realise the importance that for the international community, and we were responsible -- UNPROFOR was responsible for that -- so the importance of this very fact. Mr. Stojic, well, through his interpreter, said, "Yes, I do understand but the problem is I've done everything that I could do." So I thought that there was a means of communication, radio communication, but it seems that this wasn't the case, and the fact is that I suggested that if I helped with radio communication, he said okay,. So we asked for this from Medjugorje and I saw him exercise pressure, I saw him, but to that point, to that moment, the pressure I -- it was me who was exercising that pressure. And the situation wasn't easy for him, and the Konjic pocket had felt isolated from the HVO headquarters. I don't know whether I've been clear enough, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You have just explained, if one might summarise, that you exerted pressure on Mr. Stojic, you didn't know whether he could get this done or not. When you realised he didn't have communication with the pocket, you enabled him to have that communication, and then he continued exerting pressure on the commander of the Konjic pocket until the people were released. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the summary is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Well, we'll just dwell on this a little while longer, very briefly, do you remember whether the commander of the Konjic pocket asked for some kind of assistance from Mr. Stojic in order to release the interpreters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand what you mean by some sort of assistance. There were requests related to Konjic staff, but I don't know whether they tried to connect Konjic with the area controlled by the HVO. But I don't quite understand what you mean when talking about assistance because there was a Spanish patrol waiting to get into the pocket and to get the interpreters. I don't know whether you mean this or not. If that's what you're talking about, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I'm referring to assistance in food, medicines, and similar items that they were short of, because the very word "pocket" indicates that they were isolated and surrounded. Do you know whether they asked for any specific assistance in food or medicines, at that point from Mr. Stojic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember in detail, but obviously in the Konjic pocket all the organisations working with humanitarian aid were doing everything they could to try to help and that's why I was there in that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Sir, please let's look at a document in my binder. It's P02826. It's the third document from the top, page 2 in Croatian, page 1 in English. This is a report as we can see of UN civilian affairs. The date is the 18th of June, and I will just show you what it says at the top, that the interpreters were released on the 17th of June at 2000 hours, and then it says over the past four months, the commander in the Konjic pocket did not have any communication, he did not cooperate, he acted on his own without instructions or coordination with the HVO staff, he -- they were desperately short of food and medicine, and Mr. Stojic took on the obligation of going with me to that area in the next three months with a convoy of necessities, and the report was signed by Mr. Albert Benabou. Did you know that he was aware of this whole activity concerning the release of the interpreters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, naturally, and I can see my name on that report.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can you confirm, then, that that's precisely what happened, the commander of the Konjic pocket evidently desperately needed assistance and made use of this situation, to ask for assistance for soldiers who were encircled and who had no communication with the HVO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DV [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct what's reflected here, but one of the sentences referring to vagabonds is quite different, but I think that that's -- that's an issue that's marginal to this particular question.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll come back to Mr. Benabou later on.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I just have one more question to round off this set of questions, this topic, and then we could take a break.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Sir, I think we've clarified the questions I put at the beginning, whether the Croats in the Konjic pocket were isolated, acting without coordination with the HVO, and I think we've clarified what sort of pressure you exerted on Mr. Stojic and what sort of pressure he exerted on the commander of the Konjic pocket and what remains now is the following: You said that Mr. Stojic was the commander, but it seems to me that whether he was the commander or not, and what you mean by this, is explained in your statement of December 1997. I will read -- it's P010270. It's page 7 in English. The fourth paragraph from the top and page 7 in Croatian, the last paragraph. I will read this to you very briefly. You say, "Minister Stojic said that he did not have full control over HVO -- the HVO soldiers in the Konjic area. Owing to the fact that I enabled him to have SpaBat satellite radio equipment, he was able to issue a direct order for the hostages to be released. At that meeting, I understood that Minister Stojic was really not in control of the situation and it was very difficult for him to issue an order." Does this reflect fully the impression you gained on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Of course. It reflects the feeling that I had about him, his feeling of frustration that did he not have the means to exert his authority as minister.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. We will continue after the break and I hope that after this explanation, I won't have to go back to the Konjic pocket. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We shall have a 20 minute break and resume at 11.00 until 12.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mrs. Nozica, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I omitted to state at the beginning that I had 80 minutes for my cross-examination. My own 30 minutes, 30 minutes from Mrs. Tomasegovic, and 20 minutes from Mr. Karnavas. So according to my calculations I've used up 35 minutes thus far which leaves me with 45 minutes. Your Honour, I'm sure you're aware of the fact that I have to get through a lot of topics.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Karnavas had five minutes, so you have therefore 25 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I just wanted to say that I'll do everything possible to get through the important topics as far as the Stojic Defence is concerned. If I don't manage to do that I'll let you know, and if I can get additional time I'll be very grateful to you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, sir, I'd like to move on to another topic, Colonel Jesus Fernandez. In your statement of July 2007, and it is your statement, P10217, am I right, is everything working? We were talking about the 11th of June events, 11th of June 1993, when Lieutenant Jesus Fernandez was killed. Now, you speak about that in your report or your diary. So I'd like us to take a look at the document, it's a Prosecution document P10269. And the date is the 13th of June. Have you found that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DV [Resumed]
utterances.text: 13th of June?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Yes. Now, on that date, the 13th of June, you noted that after meeting military officials of the Croatian Defence Council, permission was granted to go to the front line in -- at the Bulevar in Mostar, and you also speak about the fact that you climbed on to the roof of the highest building on territory controlled by the Croats, and you also said that from there you photographed the areas that could be seen from that vantage point, and that empty casings were found. And you said that several hours later, this video material, photographic material, was handed over to the UNPROFOR team of international experts who were preparing an official report on the killing of the Spanish lieutenant. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perfectly.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I'd like you now to look at your operations diary, and it is P02108, and the entry for the 14th of June. For the 14th of June, this is what you say: "A meeting in Mostar between the Deputy Minister of the HVO, Ivica Lucic, and the commission, in order to clarify the cause -- or the circumstances of the death of Lieutenant Aguilar." Now, you attended this meeting; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on the 13th.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I'd like you now to take a look in my binder, document 2D 00117. And you'll find a yellow sticker in the middle of the document. Thank you. As you can see, this is a report from the meeting signed by Mr. Lucic dated the 14th of June 1993, which you mention in your diary. And your name is mentioned there as well. It says that a meeting was held and that it says, as it says here, the assistant minister and everybody present, (redacted)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're quite right. Registrar, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I think that while we are dealing with this document it would then be go a good idea to go into closed session because mention is made of the witness again, so perhaps it would be better to go into closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I haven't received an answer. I'm just referring to the fact --

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Dr. Bagaric, I mean, Dr. Bagaric. Did you have any contacts with him regarding evacuation or anything like that? You can't remember, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly, I knew him but right now I can't place a face to that name, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: In my binder, I had prepared some documents which were correspondence between the two of you. That would probably jog your memory but I won't have time to go through that, but you drew up a report, a professional report, on that dinner. Regardless of the fact that it was a private dinner, you compiled a report, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Obviously, when Mr. Soljud [phoen] had his -- explained to us of his own bad operational initiatives, then I together with the other two Spanish officers, we came up with this report, and it was a political report, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Very well. Now, can we take a look at that report of yours? May we take a look at that report of yours, P03545 is the document number. It's in the Prosecution binder. I assume that it's one of the top-most documents. 3545. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I've found it.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... Going to ask you some questions. In the report, you state the following: Mr. Stojic's words and your comments. You say that Mr. Stojic said that he was certain that his people could solve the situation, once and for all, and he confirmed the loss of territory in certain areas as part of a previously designed plan. Now, your comment to that was that Mr. Stojic might have been attempting to justify his losses at the beginning. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DV [Resumed]
utterances.text: My comment was that perhaps he was -- maybe that or maybe he was saying the truth. That's all there is to it. We thought that, yeah, maybe it could have been the truth or a justification, but maybe I should read the whole paragraph through.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Please, we all have the document in front of us and unfortunately I don't have much time. I said that it was one of your comments. You made two comments, one of which was what I read out. I don't have time to go into the whole of it, but let's try and get to the goal as soon as possible, and what I want to ask you as a final question. You go on to say that Mr. Stojic said that there was some plan to exert maximum pressure from the southern axis leaving open one communication line for the withdrawal of the forces in the direction of Jablanica towards the north, and your comment was that this pressure from the south, as well as the shelling and isolation of the Muslim part of town, would certainly make the population leave the town. Is that right? Persuade them to leave the town, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can we now move on? This is what Mr. Stojic said among other things, he's also said some other things, but let's see whether we can move on and see what was actually going on at that point in time in Mostar, and what was happening over the next 20 days. For us to be able to check and see whether Mr. Stojic was talking about a realistic plan or whether it was just justification, as you say, for territory that had almost been lost. So may we take a look at that same report of yours and look at page 8 of that report in the English version, and it is page 5 of the Croatian, where he speaks about this area of Mostar, so it is that day, and what -- let's see what was happening in Mostar. He says, "Fighting in the Mostar area continues, but their intensity is relatively low." Have you found that portion? It is the subtitle of Mostar part 1.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I found that part.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now it says under point 2 there are very few vehicles and soldiers seen moving about in that area, and then number 3, according to all the indicators, it is possible that the HVO most certainly took control of the village of Buna. Now, what I want to ask you is this: Do you know, do you have any knowledge, or awareness, of what happened on the 13th of July 1993? Or, rather, do you know that the BH army did take control of these areas on the 13th of July and that in actual fact, the operation which is described in this report of the 17th was just a counterattack to what was done by the BH army on the 13th? Did you know about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DV [Resumed]
utterances.text: On a daily basis we received a briefing of the situation. I don't remember anything coming -- information coming from the confrontation line on the 13th of June. I remember movements around the Buna village, for example, but I don't remember the details. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Sir, sir, I consider -- well, my colleague asked you about certain events that took place in Mostar, and I consider that this is the date which judging by the intensity of the operations, and I'm saying this as a layman, whereas you're a professional soldier, should be something that would you have had to have known about. But let us look at a document in my binder, P03416 is the number. It is the 6th document in line from the top. And it is a document dated the 13th of July 1993, the date is the 13th of July --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DV [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And we can look at page 2 of the English, where it says the following: "AB and B this morning attacked Buna" and on page 3 of the English version, it says, "ABH attack on Buna is perhaps an attempt to isolate Mostar from the south. If ABiH -- we succeed attacking also from the office of the HVO in Mostar will be completely isolated, cut off. On the other hand, this attack may be an army, Armija attempt to conquer as much terrain in direction to the sea as possible." I'm asking you, and I wish to jog your memory with this report: Do you know that this happened just five days before that dinner? And did you know anything about the efforts made by the BH army to gain control of the territory to the sea from the north? Did you know anything about that? The 30th of June to the 13th of July, did you or did you not? Just give me a yes or no answer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, yes. We knew that that was the Armija's objective, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Excellent. So that day, when you attended the dinner, when you were there with Mr. Stojic, having dinner, you knew that before that, several days before that, the BH army had taken control of certain territory from the south of Mostar. Can we put it that way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DV [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. That's why we understood that the idea of Mr. Stojic of this idea of losing territory temporarily might have been, I'm not sure how to say it, a justification as to why there had been these losses in the area. We knew that this was a -- the decision of the ABiH at that time. We knew that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Correct, yes, sir. That is what you say in your report. Now, I would just like to ask you to tell me this: Well, we followed the military situation, to the best of your knowledge did the HVO exert pressure from the south of Mostar to liberate the north and an exit from Mostar as Mr. Stojic said over the following 20 days or one month or in general terms, do you remember that the HVO did realise what allegedly Mr. Stojic said or boasted that the HVO would do? Do you remember any operations like that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I seem to recall that the HVO in some moments had conducted initiatives in the south, but I don't think it ever actually recovered the lost territory, not in its entirety, maybe some, but I heard this was a tactic, we weren't sure if this was a tactic or not a tactic and that's all I can say about the dinner.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Okay. You said "undertook something, did something." Is that a limited operation or an all-embracing, comprehensive operation? Could you be a bit more precise because it's very important. You say the HVO did something, undertook something. Yes, we can see from the report that it did undertake something in that direction, but can you say that the HVO undertook any large-scale offensive? Can we put it that way? Perhaps it's easiest that way? To the best of your knowledge, there were a lot of witnesses, we have established a lot of things already, but as far as you're concerned, in your opinion.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DV [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm going to be sincere. I wrote my diary because there was some reason I can't remember. I remember there was an offensive, but I don't remember the dates and I wouldn't be able to stipulate which dates, if that's your question, no. I remember there was a offensive but I don't remember the dates. At the time, if you want to know if it happened in the following 20 days, I can't confirm that, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I followed your diary and unfortunately there are a lots of notes in it about who you met with and very little information, otherwise the 30th of June was not recorded and the BH army attack on the HVO, the 13th of July. Once again there was not recorded. So it's not in your diary. If it were I would have shown you, but just finally let's look at a document linked to this topic, it is P03615 and it is a document from the Prosecution binder, 3615 is the number, once again, it has to do with the dinner. Tell me when you've found it, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I've just found it.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: We can take a look at it together. The date of the document is the 19th of July 1993. And it is in fact a message -- yes, go ahead. What did you want to say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, I can see that it's the 21st of the -- of July, 3615. It's the 21st of July; is that correct? That is a report from the meeting with Paparovi [phoen], is that what you're referring to? Yes. The one that's on the screen; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: That's right. The meeting was on the 19th of July. The meeting was on the 19th of July? Am I right? And it says report from the meeting --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And this is a writ from Berebon Flamon [phoen] and yes, the meeting took place on the 19th, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can you and I agree that the meeting was held on the 19th, which means barely two days after the dinner you had at Mr. Stojic's house? Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I would like to ask you to have a look at point 5 in this letter together. Obviously, this is a courtesy meeting. It says, "At an informal private meeting between myself and Boban," this is written by Mr. -- by General Briquemont. Immediately after the meeting he suggested that he mediate in order to have an immediate cease-fire among all the parties, and he said that this would have the unqualified support of the Croat peoples and the HVO and could be a precursor to lasting peace. Do you know what Mr. Boban's exact position was in the HVO? Did you know that he was commander in chief at the HVO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Naturally, I knew who Boban was.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So it stems from this document that Mr. Boban offered to Mr. Briquemont at that moment to have a cease-fire established, right? That is unequivocally clear on the basis of this document.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DV [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could be interpreted that way, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to conclude with two very brief questions, but could we move into private session, please, because I need to mention a few names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So we are interrupt the hearing and resume again at quarter -- half past 2.00. --- Luncheon recess taken at 12.33 p.m. --- Upon resuming at 2.29 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us resume the hearing. Mr. Kovacic, please tell us very briefly why Mr. Praljak is going to be putting questions to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I can inform you of the following. I shall be the first to put some questions to the witness, and then, with your leave, Mr. Praljak. I think that the arguments are quite obvious. The witness speaks of a series of events where Mr. Praljak was directly involved. For example, the witness himself mentioned even four or rather three events in his statement, and one is mentioned in one of the documents. These are direct encounters with Mr. Praljak, and I believe that this fits into your previous decision; namely, that Mr. Praljak should be given an opportunity to ask about various matters particularly what happened in Mostar at the time. If I may start, I am ready, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour, it seems there was some confusion with the documents, but I think he received them. Thank you. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kovacic, for my colleague, Judge Mindua, do you have a set of documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Witness, I'm going to put a few questions to you. I am Defence counsel for General Praljak who is present here. In your statement, from 2007, that is to say P02107, in paragraph 24, you said that you first saw General Praljak at a meeting held on the 29th of April in Medjugorje. You said here that also in attendance were Mr. Stojic and Mr. Bozic, and the next paragraph, 25, you say that that meeting was held in order to prepare for an official visit of a commission of the Croatian parliament to Bosnia-Herzegovina. I would like to remind you that an identical statement is made in document 10269, in the notes for the 29th of April, and the 2nd of May 1993. My question is as follows: Let us try to save time. On the basis of these entries, paragraphs 24 and 25 in P2107, can we conclude that this meeting was held in order to do what is necessary or, rather, in order to prepare the official visit of the delegation of the Croatian parliament to Bosnia-Herzegovina? A yes or a no answer will suffice.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DV [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I would like to ask you to look at a document that is in my binder, that is the first one, 3D 00566.
